signals.title: NOK/NZD — G10 Bilateral Theme + Macro Divergence
signals.text: The G10 scorecard shows NOK outperforming with a 1W average gain of +1.469% across 2 pairs, while NZD lags with a -0.594% average across 4 pairs, creating a critical 2.063% bilateral spread. Geopolitical tension from Strait of Hormuz tanker disruptions keeps WTI elevated at $102.3, bolstering the energy-linked Norwegian Krone. In contrast, New Zealand macro data shows acute weakness, reflected in a negative ESI reading of -18.1 compared to Norway's positive +14.9. Furthermore, Norges Bank policy rate sits at 4.50% with an inflation expectation of 2.68% delivering a +1.82% restrictive real rate, compared to RBNZ at 2.75% with a +0.41% real rate. This cross-macro spread drives sustained divergence between the G10 leader and laggard. Trade bias: Bullish NOK/NZD; macro and terms-of-trade divergence favors sustained outperformance. Catalyst: New Zealand Employment Change release at 21:45 UTC. Risk: Strait of Hormuz shipping lane reopens abruptly, triggering a sharp decline in crude prices and compressing the bilateral spread below 1.20%.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Vol Premium + Options Downside Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 157.65, holding below its SMA20 at 157.90 and below its SMA200 at 158.48, with the deterministic trend structure confirming an active downtrend. 1M implied volatility sits at 7.4% against a 30-day realized volatility of 5.2%, generating an elevated Vol Risk Premium of +2.1%. The options market demonstrates heavy downside hedging demand, with 25-delta risk reversals printing an extreme put skew of -2.24. While Fed SOFR at 3.94% vs BoJ TONA at 1.23% delivers a +271bp carry advantage that favors USD, option desks are paying a premium for downside protection against verbal or physical MoF intervention. Watch for spot testing 157.41 (SMA50) to confirm if options-led selling accelerates. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY; elevated options put skew indicates downside hedging pressure despite positive carry. Catalyst: next BoJ meeting (mkt: 69% hike priced) to assess policy shift. Risk: US ISM Manufacturing PMI prints well above the 54.7 forecast, pushing US yields higher and lifting USD/JPY through 158.48.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Crowded Short + Retail Divergence
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1161, remaining pinned below its SMA20 at 1.1201, SMA50 at 1.1392, and SMA200 at 1.1567 in an established technical downtrend. CFTC positioning shows institutional Leveraged Funds net short EUR by -99,557 contracts, residing at the 2nd percentile of its 52-week range with a z-score of -1.78. Conversely, retail sentiment on Retail sentiment data indicates extreme positioning with 86% of retail traders long, diverging sharply from the institutional short stance. Fed SOFR at 3.94% vs ECB €STR at 2.44% delivers a +150bp carry differential favoring USD, keeping structural pressure on the pair. The clash between crowded institutional shorts and trapped retail longs creates vulnerability to a sharp squeeze if resistance breaks. Trade bias: Short EUR/USD; institutional positioning and carry favor USD while retail remains trapped on the long side. Catalyst: US ISM Manufacturing PMI at 15:00 UTC. Risk: EUR/USD clears the SMA20 at 1.1201, prompting leveraged fund profit-taking and triggering a positioning short squeeze.

signals.title: AUD/USD — RBA Decision + Technical Resistance
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7030, holding above its SMA20 at 0.6996 but facing heavy overhead resistance at the SMA200 (0.7060) and SMA50 (0.7069). RBA AONIA at 4.60% vs Fed SOFR at 3.94% generates a -66bp carry advantage favoring the Australian Dollar. However, China's factory and services PMIs both contracted below 50 over the weekend, and domestic factory PMI slipped to 49.6, softening the external backdrop. CFTC Leveraged Funds sit net long AUD by +43,927 contracts, but positioning growth is stalling with a WoW reduction of -3,679 contracts. The technical structure flags reversal risk against the downtrend as spot approaches the steep 200-day moving average. Trade bias: Neutral/range AUD/USD; supportive cash carry confronts technical resistance and softer manufacturing data. Catalyst: RBA Interest Rate Decision and Monetary Policy Statement at 04:30 UTC. Risk: RBA unexpectedly signals an extended pause rather than maintaining its hiking bias, breaking spot below the SMA20 support at 0.6996.
